profile.campus: Gainesville, Prince William County, Virginia (Microsoft data center land, Data Center Opportunity Zone)
profile.address: 13760 University Boulevard, Gainesville, Prince William County, Virginia, 20155
profile.reading:
This site is part of Microsoft's Gainesville, Prince William County, Virginia data center footprint. Data Center Dynamics reported that in March 2024 Microsoft paid $465.5 million, roughly $3.75 million per acre, for about 124 acres across two parcels at 13490 University Boulevard and 5941 Wellington Road, bought from local landowner Chuck Kuhn's JK Land Holdings; Kuhn's company had acquired the same site for just $46.9 million in 2020, illustrating how sharply Prince William County data center land values rose over that period. The parcels sit within the county's designated Data Center Opportunity Zone, and a pending rezoning application at the time of the DCD report sought increased density allowances for up to 3.8 million square feet of data center use plus a new electrical substation. Microsoft's Gainesville acquisition placed it near competing hyperscale investments: Amazon owns an adjacent 117-acre site planned for a 2.3-million-square-foot campus, and a Google-linked entity, Sharpless Enterprises, has been developing a nearby campus of its own, while Microsoft separately held 92.6 acres in nearby Bristow from a 2021 acquisition. Local outlet InsideNoVa has also reported public comment periods and community transparency concerns around Microsoft's Prince William County data center plans, including one sited on a former missile facility. Microsoft has not publicly confirmed a development timeline, building count, or individual building square footage for this specific Gainesville site, so this registry records the 3.8-million-square-foot rezoning request as the upper-bound regional context rather than a confirmed building-level fact.

Dominion Energy, the regional utility serving Loudoun and Prince William counties, has repeatedly cited Northern Virginia data center growth as the largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory in filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission, prompting new transmission and generation investment; Virginia's data center sales-and-use tax exemption, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership, has been a material factor cited by state and local officials in why Microsoft and other hyperscalers have concentrated so much investment in this specific corridor rather than spreading it across lower-tax states.

reading.body:
Microsoft purchased 124 acres in Prince William County's Data Center Opportunity Zone in March 2024 for $465.5 million, roughly $3.75 million per acre. A rezoning request submitted at the time of purchase sought approval for up to 3.8 million square feet of data center use plus a new electrical substation on the site. Microsoft has not published a development timeline, building count, individual power capacity, or confirmation that construction has begun as of September 2026.

The site sits within a dense cluster of competing hyperscale investments in Gainesville. Amazon owns an adjacent 117-acre parcel planned for 2.3 million square feet, and a Google-linked entity is developing a nearby campus. Land values in the corridor have risen roughly tenfold since 2020, driven by data center demand and Virginia's sales-and-use tax exemption for data centers. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has cited Northern Virginia data center growth as the largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory.

Virginia has 23 data centers with published power capacity totaling 1,375 megawatts across 326 mapped facilities statewide. This Gainesville campus does not yet rank among the 23 published, since no individual power figure has been disclosed. Without a confirmed power allocation or building schedule, the site cannot be assessed against other Virginia capacity today, though the rezoning request and land acquisition signal intent to add material compute load to an already constrained regional grid.
